_comment: pillars.json — v0.8 schema example (additive-only since v0.4). Pillars are the 3-5 commitments the game makes to its players. Every milestone in milestones.json must bind to ≥1 pillar via `pillars_targeted`. Anti-examples are pre-committed phrases that mark pillar violations — fired by gmk-self-test code matching during play sessions. supported_genres_check is read by gmk-shape-advisor and gmk-portability-check to determine bot-validation confidence. kit_version is read v0.7+ per gmk-prototype-rules Rule 16 (warn-only on future versions). pillars[].kind is read v0.8+ per gmk-prototype-rules Rule 17 (4-value enum: sensory/behavioral/decision-shape/emotional; free-text fallback if absent).

pillars.name: Every merge feels mechanical and chunky
pillars.description: Hit-stop, screen shake, particle burst, audio thud — the merge resolves with weight. The player physically registers each combine.
anti_examples: merges that happen off-screen without feedback

pillars.name: Each new species is a surprise worth waiting for
pillars.description: Distinct silhouette, distinct color, distinct animation. The next dragon should not look like a recolor of the previous one.
anti_examples: species that aren't visually grouped into eras / families

pillars.name: Death-to-next-attempt is under 2 seconds
pillars.description: After death (or run end), the player is back to interactive mid-board within 2 seconds. No menus, no confirmations, no animations.
anti_examples: game-over screen that requires a click

supported_genres_check._comment_check: All three true → standard bot validation confidence. Any false → gmk-validate adds a caveat (bot signal is reduced for this milestone).
